text: pH of water is 7 at $25^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. If water is heated to $80^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$., it's pH will :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The self-ionisation of water, $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\qquad \mathrm{H}{}^{+}+\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}$, is endothermic, so $K_{w}$ increases on heating: from $1.0\times 10^{-14}$ at $25^{\circ }\text{C}$ to about $2.5\times 10^{-13}$ ($\text{p}K_{w}\approx 12.6$) at $80^{\circ }\text{C}$.

In pure water $[\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]=[\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}]=\sqrt{K_{w}}$ at every temperature, so both concentrations increase equally and the water remains neutral.

Since $\text{pH}=-\log [\mathrm{H}{}^{+}]=\frac{1}{2}\text{p}K_{w}$, the pH falls below 7 (about 6.3 at $80^{\circ }\text{C}$).

Option (D) is wrong because $[\mathrm{OH}{}^{-}]$ also increases.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: When a non-volatile solute is added to the solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreases by 10 mm of Hg . The mole fraction of the solute in the solution is 0.2 . What would be the mole fraction of the solvent if decrease in vapour pressure is 20 mm of Hg ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When a non-volatile solute is added to a solvent, it causes the vapour pressure of the solvent to decrease. In this scenario, when the vapour pressure decreases by 10 mm of Hg, the mole fraction of the solute in the solution is 0.2. 

By understanding the relationship between vapour pressure change and mole fraction, we see that:

The change in vapour pressure ($P^{\circ }-P$) is directly proportional to the mole fraction of the solute ($X_{\text{solute}}$).

Therefore, if a 10 mm of Hg decrease corresponds to a mole fraction of 0.2, then a 20 mm of Hg decrease would correspond to a mole fraction of 0.4.

To find the mole fraction of the solvent ($X_{\text{solvent}}$), we use the formula:

$X_{\text{solvent}}=1-X_{\text{solute}}$

Substituting the value we found:

$X_{\text{solvent}}=1-0.4=0.6$

Thus, when the vapour pressure decreases by 20 mm of Hg, the mole fraction of the solvent is 0.6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: Consider a binary solution of two volatile liquid components 1 and $2.x_{1}$ and $y_{1}$ are the mole fractions of component 1 in liquid and vapour phase, respectively. The slope and intercept of the linear plot of $\frac{1}{x_{1}}$ vs $\frac{1}{y_{1}}$ are given respectively as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a binary solution of two volatile liquid components labeled 1 and 2, let $x_{1}$ and $y_{1}$ represent the mole fractions of component 1 in the liquid and vapor phases, respectively. The linear relationship between the inverse of these mole fractions is plotted as $\frac{1}{x_{1}}$ versus $\frac{1}{y_{1}}$.

To derive the slope and intercept of this linear plot, consider the following calculations:

Using Raoult's Law for a Liquid Solution:

For a liquid solution with volatile components 1 and 2:

$\mathrm{P}_{1}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}\cdot y_{1}=\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}\cdot x_{1}$

Therefore:

$\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}}{x_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{y_{1}}$

Rearranging the Equation:

By substituting and rearranging, we have:

$\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}+x_{1}(\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}-\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}})}{x_{1}}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{y_{1}}$

Simplifying further:

$\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}}{x_{1}}+(\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}-\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}})=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{y_{1}}$

Expressing $\frac{1}{x_{1}}$:

Solving for $\frac{1}{x_{1}}$, we obtain:

$\frac{1}{x_{1}}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}}\right )\left (\frac{1}{y_{1}}\right )+\left (\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}-\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}}\right )$

Determining the Slope and Intercept:

The slope of the line is:

$\text{Slope}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}}$

The intercept of the line is:

$\text{Intercept}=\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}-\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}}$

In summary, for the plot of $\frac{1}{x_{1}}$ against $\frac{1}{y_{1}}$, the slope is $\frac{\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}}$ and the intercept is $\frac{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}-\mathrm{P}_{1}^{\mathrm{o}}}{\mathrm{P}_{2}^{\mathrm{o}}}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

solution.body:

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement (I) : The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increase in the number of C -atoms.

Statement (II) : The boiling points of alcohols and phenols are higher in comparison to other class of compounds such as ethers, haloalkanes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement (I):

As the number of carbon atoms in alcohols or phenols increases, the molecule becomes larger, which in turn enhances the van der Waals (dispersion) forces between the molecules.

Stronger intermolecular forces require more energy (i.e., higher temperature) to overcome, leading to higher boiling points.

Therefore, Statement (I) is true.

Statement (II):

Alcohols and phenols have a hydroxyl group ($-OH$) that can form hydrogen bonds, which are significantly stronger than the dipole-dipole interactions typically seen in ethers or the interactions in haloalkanes.

This stronger hydrogen bonding means that alcohols and phenols have higher boiling points compared to ethers and haloalkanes of similar molecular weight.

Hence, Statement (II) is also true.

Based on the above points, the correct answer is:

Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text: The $α$-Helix and $β$ - Pleated sheet structures of protein are associated with its :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The secondary structure of a protein is the shape in which its long polypeptide chain is held by hydrogen bonds between the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{H}$ groups of the peptide bonds.

Its two common forms are the $α$-helix, in which the chain coils into a right-handed helix held by hydrogen bonds within the same chain, and the $β$-pleated sheet, in which chains lie side by side and are held by hydrogen bonds between neighbouring chains.

The primary structure is only the sequence of amino acids, while the tertiary and quaternary structures describe the folding of the whole chain and the arrangement of several subunits.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
The effect of temperature on spontaneity of reactions are represented as :

  
    
    $\Delta$H
    $\Delta$S
    Temperature
    Spontaneity
  

  
    (A)
    $+$
    $-$
    any T
    Non spontaneous
  
  
    (B)
    $+$
    $+$
    low T
    spontaneous
  
  
    (C)
    $-$
    $-$
    low T
    Non spontaneous
  
  
    (D)
    $-$
    $+$
    any T
    spontaneous
  

The incorrect combinations are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let's analyze each combination using the Gibbs free energy equation:

$\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$

A reaction is spontaneous when $\Delta G<0.$ 

Now, consider each case:

(A) $\Delta H>0$ and $\Delta S<0$  

Here, $\Delta G=+\text{(positive)}-T(-\text{(positive)})=\text{positive}+T\text{(positive)}$  

This is positive for any temperature.  

Thus, the reaction is non-spontaneous for any T, which is correct.

(B) $\Delta H>0$ and $\Delta S>0$  

Now, $\Delta G=+\text{(positive)}-T\text{(positive)}.$  

For $\Delta G$ to be negative, the temperature has to be high enough such that $T\Delta S>\Delta H.$  

The table incorrectly states that the reaction is spontaneous at low T.

(C) $\Delta H<0$ and $\Delta S<0$  

In this case, $\Delta G=-\text{(positive)}-T(-\text{(positive)})=-\text{(positive)}+T\text{(positive)}.$  

At very low temperatures, the term $T\Delta S$ is small, making $\Delta G$ negative (spontaneous).  

The table mistakenly indicates that the reaction is non-spontaneous at low T.

(D) $\Delta H<0$ and $\Delta S>0$  

Then, $\Delta G=-\text{(positive)}-T\text{(positive)}.$  

This expression is negative at all temperatures, so the reaction is correctly marked as spontaneous.

Thus, the incorrect combinations are:

(B): It should be spontaneous at high T, not low T.

(C): It should be spontaneous at low T, not non-spontaneous.

Therefore, the incorrect combinations are (B) and (C) only.

The correct answer is Option D.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ozonolysis with reductive work-up ($\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$, then $\mathrm{Zn}/\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$) cleaves every C=C into two C=O groups: a doubly bonded carbon carrying two carbon substituents becomes a ketone C=O, and a $=\mathrm{CH}{}^{-}$ carbon becomes $-\mathrm{CHO}$.

Each isomer is a methyl-substituted bicyclic diene with one C=C at the ring fusion; cleaving the fusion C=C and the second C=C opens both rings, so each isomer gives a single tetracarbonyl compound containing all 10 carbons.

(A) has the methyl on the middle carbon of the five-membered ring and its second C=C in the six-membered ring next to the fusion, giving $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CHO}$, which is (III).

(B) has its second C=C in the five-membered ring next to the fusion with the methyl on the outer carbon of that C=C, giving $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CO}-(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}){}_{4}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, which is (IV).

(C) has the methyl on the six-membered ring and its second C=C in the six-membered ring next to the fusion, giving $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CO}-(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}){}_{3}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CHO}$, which is (I).

(D) has its second C=C in the five-membered ring with the methyl on the carbon next to the fusion, giving $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CO}-(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}){}_{4}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CHO}$, which is (II).

The matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

text:
Identify the coordination complexes in which the central metal ion has $\mathrm{d}^{4}$ configuration.

(A) $[\mathrm{FeO}_{4}]^{2-}$

(B) $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$

(C) $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]^{3-}$

(D) 
[IMG]

(E) $[\mathrm{NiF}_{6}]^{2-}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The oxidation state of the metal fixes its d-electron count.

(A) $[\mathrm{FeO}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $x+4(-2)=-2\Rightarrow x=+6$; $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{6+}$ is $3d^{2}$.

(B) $[\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $x+6(-1)=-3\Rightarrow x=+3$; $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{4}$.

(C) $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $x+6(-1)=-3\Rightarrow x=+3$; $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{5}$.

(D) $[\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COO}){}_{4}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{2}]$ is neutral with four acetate ions ($-1$ each) shared by two Cr atoms, so $2x-4=0\Rightarrow x=+2$; $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{4}$.

(E) $[\mathrm{NiF}{}_{6}]{}^{2-}$: $x+6(-1)=-2\Rightarrow x=+4$; $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{4+}$ is $3d^{6}$.

Only complexes (B) and (D) have the $d^{4}$ configuration.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
Consider the reaction

$\mathrm{X}_{2}\mathrm{Y}(\mathrm{g})⇌\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

The equation representing correct relationship between the degree of dissociation (x) of $\mathrm{X}_{2}\mathrm{Y}(\mathrm{g})$ with its equilibrium constant Kp is $__________$.

Assume $x$ to be very very small.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the relationship between the degree of dissociation ($x$) of $\mathrm{X}_{2}\mathrm{Y}(\mathrm{g})$ and its equilibrium constant $K_{p}$, let's analyze the reaction:

$\mathrm{X}_{2}\mathrm{Y}(\mathrm{g})⇌\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Y}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

Initial and Change in Moles

Initially, we start with 1 mole of $\mathrm{X}_{2}\mathrm{Y}$.

At equilibrium:

$\mathrm{X}_{2}\mathrm{Y}$ is $(1-x)$ moles. 

$\mathrm{X}_{2}$ is $x$ moles. 

$\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Y}_{2}$ is $\frac{x}{2}$ moles.

Partial Pressures
The total pressure $\mathrm{P}_{\text{total}}$ is given by:

$\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{X}_{2}\mathrm{Y}}=\frac{1-x}{1+\frac{x}{2}}\times \mathrm{P}$

$\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{X}_{2}}=\frac{x}{1+\frac{x}{2}}\times \mathrm{P}$

$\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{Y}_{2}}=\frac{x/2}{1+\frac{x}{2}}\times \mathrm{P}$

Equilibrium Constant Expression
The equilibrium constant $K_{p}$ can be written in terms of partial pressures:

$K_{p}=\frac{\left (\frac{x}{1+\dfrac{x}{2}}\cdot \mathrm{P}\right )\cdot \left (\frac{\dfrac{x}{2}}{1+\dfrac{x}{2}}\cdot \mathrm{P}\right )^{1/2}}{\frac{1-x}{1+\dfrac{x}{2}}\cdot \mathrm{P}}$

Simplifying the expression, considering $x$ to be very small, results in:

$K_{p}=\left (\frac{x}{1-x}\right )\left (\frac{x}{2\left (1+\frac{x}{2}\right )}\right )^{1/2}\cdot \mathrm{P}^{\frac{1}{2}}$

For small $x$, $(1-x)\approx 1$, thus:

$K_{p}=\frac{x^{3/2}}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \mathrm{P}^{\frac{1}{2}}$

$x^{3/2}=\frac{K_{p}\cdot 2^{1/2}}{\mathrm{P}^{1/2}}$

Finally, by squaring both sides:

$x^{3}=\frac{2\cdot K_{p}^{2}}{\mathrm{P}}$

$x=\left (\frac{2\cdot K_{p}^{2}}{\mathrm{P}}\right )^{1/3}$

Thus, the degree of dissociation $x$ relates to $K_{p}$ by the equation:

$x=\left (\frac{2\cdot K_{p}^{2}}{\mathrm{P}}\right )^{1/3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

solution.body:
Solvolysis of these bromides follows the $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}1$ path, so the rate follows the stability of the carbocation formed when $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ leaves.

(C), bromodiphenylmethane, gives $(\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}^{+}$, whose charge is delocalised over two benzene rings: the most stable cation.

(B), 1-bromo-4-methyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydronaphthalene, gives a secondary benzylic cation, held coplanar with the fused benzene ring and delocalised into it.

(A), 1-bromo-1,4,4-trimethylcyclohexane, gives a tertiary alkyl cation stabilised only by hyperconjugation and the $+I$ effect, which is weaker than benzylic resonance.

(D), 2-bromo-3-methylpentane, gives a secondary alkyl cation: the least stable.

The ascending order of rate is $(\text{D})<(\text{A})<(\text{B})<(\text{C})$.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: 0.01 mole of an organic compound $(X)$ containing $10%$ hydrogen, on complete combustion produced $0.9\mathrm{g}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$. Molar mass of $(\mathrm{X})$ is $_________$ $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Organic compound $\leftarrow ^{\text{combustion}}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{\begin{array}{l} 0.9\mathrm{gm} \end{array}}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \therefore \text{mole of}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}=\dfrac{0.9}{18}=0.05\text{mole} \\ \begin{array}{ll} \therefore \text{mole of}\mathrm{H}\text{in}\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} & =0.05\times 2=0.1\text{mole} \\ =\text{mole of}\mathrm{H}\text{in}0.01\text{mole} \\ \text{Organic compound} \end{array} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \begin{array}{ll} \therefore \text{wt of}\mathrm{H}\text{atom in}0.01\text{mole compound} & =0.1\times 1 \\ =0.1\mathrm{gm} \end{array} \\ \therefore \text{wt of}\mathrm{H}\text{atom in one mole compound} \\ \begin{array}{l} =\dfrac{0.1}{0.01}=10\mathrm{gm} \\ \because \text{wt.}%\text{of}H=\dfrac{\text{wt. of}H\text{in one mole compound}}{\text{Molar mass of compound}}\times 100 \\ 10=\dfrac{10}{M}\times 100 \\ \therefore M=100 \end{array} \end{array}$

text:
The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{X}_{2}\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\text{bond}}^{\circ }$ calculated from the given data is $___________$ $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{M}^{+}\mathrm{X}^{-}(\mathrm{s})\to \mathrm{M}^{+}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{X}^{-}(\mathrm{g})\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\text{lattice}}^{\circ }=800\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \\ \mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})\to \mathrm{M}(\mathrm{g})\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\text{sub}}^{\circ }=100\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1} \end{array}$

$\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{M}^{+}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{e}^{-}(\mathrm{g})\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{i}}^{\circ }=500\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{e}^{-}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{X}^{-}(\mathrm{g})\Delta \mathrm{H}_{\mathrm{eg}}^{\circ }=-300\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{s})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{X}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{M}^{+}\mathrm{X}^{-}(\mathrm{s})\Delta \mathrm{H}_{f}^{\circ }=-400\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

[Given : $\mathrm{M}^{+}\mathrm{X}^{-}$ is a pure ionic compound and X forms a diatomic molecule $\mathrm{X}_{2}$ in gaseous state]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The given lattice enthalpy refers to $\mathrm{M}{}^{+}\mathrm{X}{}^{-}(\mathrm{s})\longrightarrow \mathrm{M}{}^{+}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{X}{}^{-}(\mathrm{g})$, $\Delta H=+800\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, so forming the solid from the gaseous ions, $\mathrm{M}{}^{+}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{X}{}^{-}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{M}{}^{+}\mathrm{X}{}^{-}(\mathrm{s})$, has $\Delta H=-800\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.


[IMG]

By Hess's law, the formation enthalpy equals the sum of the steps of the cycle:

$\Delta _{f}H^{\circ }=\Delta _{sub}H^{\circ }+\Delta _{i}H^{\circ }+\frac{1}{2}\Delta _{bond}H^{\circ }+\Delta _{eg}H^{\circ }-\Delta _{lattice}H^{\circ }$

$-400=100+500+\frac{1}{2}\Delta _{bond}H^{\circ }-300-800=-500+\frac{1}{2}\Delta _{bond}H^{\circ }$

$\frac{1}{2}\Delta _{bond}H^{\circ }=100\Rightarrow \Delta _{bond}H^{\circ }=200\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 200.

text:
When 81.0 g of aluminium is allowed to react with 128.0 g of oxygen gas, the mass of aluminium oxide produced in grams is $________ . ($Nearest integer)

Given :

Molar mass of Al is $27.0\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Molar mass of O is $16.0\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the mass of aluminum oxide produced, we first consider the chemical reaction between aluminum and oxygen:

$4\text{Al}+3\text{O}_{2}\to 2\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$

Given:

Molar mass of Al = 27.0 g/mol

Molar mass of O = 16.0 g/mol

81.0 g of Al and 128.0 g of O${}_{2}$

Calculating moles of reactants:

For aluminum (Al), using its molar mass:

$\frac{81\text{g}}{27\text{g/mol}}=3\text{moles of Al}$

For oxygen (O${}_{2}$), using its molar mass (O${}_{2}$ is composed of two oxygen atoms):

$\frac{128\text{g}}{32\text{g/mol}}=4\text{moles of O}_{2}$

Identifying the limiting reagent:

From the stoichiometry of the reaction:

4 moles of Al react with 3 moles of O${}_{2}$

3 moles of Al require $\frac{3}{4}\times 3$ moles of O${}_{2}$ = 2.25 moles of O${}_{2}$

Since only 2.25 moles of O${}_{2}$ are needed by 3 moles of Al, and we have 4 moles of O${}_{2}$, aluminum is the limiting reagent.

Calculating moles of $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ formed:

From the reaction, 4 moles of Al yield 2 moles of $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$. Thus:

$\frac{3}{4}\times 2=\frac{3}{2}\text{moles of}\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$

Calculating mass of $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$:

The molar mass of $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ is:

$(2\times 27)+(3\times 16)=102\text{g/mol}$

So, the mass of $\frac{3}{2}$ moles of $\text{Al}_{2}\text{O}_{3}$ is:

$\frac{3}{2}\times 102=153\text{grams}$

Thus, the mass of aluminum oxide produced is 153 grams.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift

solution.body:
$\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{2}$/HCl at $0\text{–}5{}^{\circ }\text{C}$ diazotises 4-ethoxyaniline to the diazonium chloride A, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$.

A couples with phenol in NaOH at the position para to OH, and dilute HCl then gives B, 4-ethoxy-4'-hydroxyazobenzene, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{OH}$ ($\mathrm{C}{}_{14}\mathrm{H}{}_{14}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$).

NaOH converts the phenolic OH of B into phenoxide, which $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Br}$ ethylates (Williamson synthesis), giving C, 4,4'-diethoxyazobenzene, $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{N}=\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}-\mathrm{OC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}$ ($\mathrm{C}{}_{16}\mathrm{H}{}_{18}\mathrm{N}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$).


[IMG]

The 12 ring carbons of C are $sp^{2}$; the $sp^{3}$ carbons are the two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ and the two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ carbons of the ethoxy groups.

Hence, the answer is 4.

text:
A compound ' $\mathrm{X}$ ' absorbs 2 moles of hydrogen and ' X ' upon oxidation with $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}|\mathrm{H}^{+}$ gives


[IMG]


The total number of $σ$ bonds present in the compound ' $X$ ' is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2025 (Online) 23rd January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Absorption of 2 mol $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ shows two C=C bonds. The products account for all the carbon: acetone (3 C), acetic acid (2 C) and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COOH}$ (5 C), 10 C in all.

$\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}/\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ converts $\mathrm{R}_{2}\mathrm{C}=$ into a ketone $\mathrm{R}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{RCH}=$ into an acid $\mathrm{RCOOH}$. So acetone comes from $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}\mathrm{C}=$, acetic acid from $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}=$, and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{COOH}$ from a $=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}=$ unit in the middle of the chain.

Joining the pieces gives X as $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ or $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, both $\mathrm{C}{}_{10}\mathrm{H}{}_{18}$:


[IMG]

Either X is acyclic with $10+18=28$ atoms, so it has $28-1=27$ $σ$ bonds (each C=C contributes one $σ$ bond): 18 C–H and 9 C–C.

$18+9=27$

Hence, the answer is 27.
